**Supersedes #43.** Same content, new base. #43 went `CONFLICTING` after #44 (Cockpit v2 design bundle + PH5 roadmap) and #45 (S10 `/api/fleet-structure`) landed; force-push is blocked for agents, so the branch is replayed onto `ce5e254` rather than rebased in place. #43 will be closed with a pointer here once this merges.

Roadmap-Ref: rm:rm-l1-morning-cockpit#S9

Movement proposal: ns:l1-morning-cockpit#P3 55% -> 60% — evidence: S9's full deliverable is on this branch and browser-verified against live data (196 beads, dolt + handoff adapters up): the Leo | Northstar tab strip renders, `ui.selectedRepo` re-scopes the Northstar thread on fleet-tile selection (`Northstar · morning-cockpit` → `Northstar · cv-builder`), chat-store threads are keyed by (tab, unit) with the v1 flat file migrating into `leo`, `chatOpen` is reconciled into `mc.cockpit.v1` and survives a full reload, `buildNorthstarPreload` builds per-unit grounding from the existing `DeliverySnapshot`, and `?tab=`/`?repo=` are honoured on the chat routes. `.claude/northstar.md` `current:` is deliberately untouched — the odometer is the merge ritual's to write (core TD-008).

## Two commits, deliberately split

**`59fd67a` — #43's content, replayed.** A content-identical cherry-pick of `3805710`. The merge commit `6d0beb3` is *not* replayed: its entire contribution over `3805710` was `0e7ab49` (S9B), already on main via #42, plus the roadmap union. Every S9-touched code file is byte-identical to #43's tip except `packages/shared/src/index.ts`, which additively keeps main's S10 fleet-structure exports alongside S9's chat exports.

Both conflicts resolved per the standing rules:

- `.claude/roadmap.md` — union of both sides, ids immutable, nothing renumbered. Phases keep **both PH4 and PH5**, in that order, and main's now-false `# PH4 intentionally skipped: a concurrent main-checkout WIP may be minting it` comment is dropped — this *is* that WIP. Slice order `S1–S9, S9B, S10–S17`; PH4 prose appended after the PH3 section.
- `implementation-notes.md` — both sides appended deviations at the same position. Kept in numeric order **#14, #15** (this branch), **#16, #17, #18** (main).

**`0243af8` — the chat-store fix + slice bookkeeping.**

### An unreadable thread file must not read as an empty one

A corrupt `chat-threads.json` took the **same branch** as an absent one — fall through to the v1 flat file, return `{}` when it is empty — and the next `appendExchange` wrote that `{}` back over the top. One unparseable byte silently erased every sibling thread. This was reachable today, not hypothetically: live `.data/` holds three threads (`leo`, `northstar:morning-cockpit`, `northstar:core`) and the v1 file is already `[]`.

Absent and unreadable are now different cases. `ENOENT` still migrates v1 into `leo`, unchanged. Unparseable, wrong-shape, or otherwise unreadable moves the bytes aside to `chat-threads.corrupt-<ts>.json` (renamed, never deleted — it is the only copy of those threads) and refuses every write for the life of the process, with an explicit reason. Both call sites already handled a throw (`routes/chat.ts:270` warns and drops the exchange; the clear route surfaces a 500).

Also retires the v1 file: once the migrated map is persisted, `chat-history.json` becomes `chat-history.migrated.json`, so the legacy path can never fire twice.

Driven against a live server, not only in tests:

```
healthy read  northstar:core  → {"messages":[{"content":"core-question",...}]}
corrupt the file, then:
  GET    /api/chat/history?tab=leo            → {"messages":[]}
  DELETE /api/chat/history?tab=northstar&repo=core
    → 500 {"error":"chat history is read-only: chat-threads.json is not valid JSON;
            moved aside to chat-threads.corrupt-2026-09-24T22-14-16-953Z.json"}
  .data/ → chat-threads.corrupt-<ts>.json (19 bytes, the exact original)
           chat-threads.json is GONE, not overwritten with {}
```

Before the fix that single DELETE destroyed `leo` and `northstar:morning-cockpit`.

### Roadmap bookkeeping

- **S9 `ready` → `delivered`.**
- **S19 registered `queued`** — deviation #15's adapter work, which had no ticket anywhere. `adapters/delivery.ts:36` surfaces only northstar+roadmap **pairs** by design, so the Northstar tab cannot tell "no northstar" from "northstar without a roadmap" (6 of 19 registry entries). Filed as a slice rather than a GitHub issue: this repo has never opened one, and its own delivery pane reads roadmaps. `S18` is reserved for the S9B id-lint fix, which ships separately.
- **S13's entrance** cites the slice ref plus PR provenance; the number lands in a follow-up commit on this branch.

### Deviations logged (#19–#21)

The brief's three "sibling worktrees" were PNG screenshots and the merge commit was a no-op; the "pre-existing" roadmap-lint `S9B` error was **latent**, because the linter reads the working tree and the live clone was two commits behind; and the running cockpit has been serving with `dolt-bead` **down** on a stale S6-era `COCKPIT_DOLT_PORT=3398` override while the real Dolt server holds 269 beads on the code-default 3307.

## Gates

`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` · `pnpm build` · `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm --filter @cockpit/server contract:check` — all green.
Suite: **shared 166, watch 64, server 49** (44 + 5 new corrupt-file regressions), **renderer 24** = 303, with `CORE_REPO` set for the ADR-0013 drift gate.

Browser-verified on a scratch port (3041/5182) with the live clone left running and untouched; console clean, no errors or warnings. ADR-0005's handoff write path is not touched, and no new write path is added — the quarantine rename and v1 retirement are both cockpit-own `.data/`, the same class as `chat-threads.json` itself.
